reason: E1 directly supports that a Pt-rich HEA surface adjusts *O and *OH adsorption energies, but it concerns ORR, not ethanol oxidation, and attributes effects partly to N-doping, not solely to non-noble metals. E2 mentions an HEA catalyzing 12-electron ethanol oxidation and notes heterogeneous electronic structures, but provides no specific evidence on how Pt–Ni/Co synergy optimizes intermediate binding or C–C cleavage. The key mechanistic link between non-noble metal content and complete oxidation selectivity is thus largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Pt-rich HEA surface adjusts adsorption energies of *O and *OH, enhancing electron transfer efficiency
Non-noble metals (Ni, Co) in HEA create heterogeneous surface sites with differing electronic structure
Synergistic electronic interplay between Pt and non-noble metals optimizes binding of oxygenated intermediates
This optimization facilitates complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation (dehydrogenation and C–C bond cleavage)
Reducing non-noble metal content disrupts electronic balance, leading to partial oxidation pathways
